TREC RAG 2026

Single-pass and multi-stage answer generation, traced through one request

Nidhin Pattaniyil · Tanwir Zaman · Semih Yagli — NP Labs

2026-11-16

What the track asks

The task

The architecture

How it works · the five pieces

Plan once, search wide, narrow to evidence, then write twice. The one variable in this talk is the last box — given identical evidence, does writing once differ from writing, auditing and revising?

The request we will follow

The example · rag2026-18 · one of the 119

Six weeks of housing for a family of three — without booking something illegal or unreliable.

Our family of three may need furnished temporary housing in New York City for about six weeks while our apartment is repaired.

… Airbnb/Vrbo, an extended-stay hotel, corporate housing, or a short sublet?

… how should we compare the real costs, safety, cancellation risk, space, location, and day-to-day practicality,

… especially with a child and remote work needs?

Eight things asked at once. Hold on to the two bold facts — they sit in different sentences, and only one of the two answers ever joins them.

Planning: how it works

How it works

The instruction’s own words: “Do not answer the topic.” The planner proposes searches, never findings — it never sees a document and is never called again. At most 25 searches per topic.

Searching: how it works

How it works

One lane of seventeen, and the ≤ on each number is a cap I configured. Three orders of magnitude of text, cut down to about a page.

Evidence and nuggets: how it works

How it works

A short-term rental in New York City is one of fewer than 30 consecutive days. New York City defines a short-term rental as a stay under 30 consecutive days.

cosine 0.94 — above 0.92, so these count as one passage. The stronger one survives in its original wording; the other is dropped.

Both writers then get one frozen package: the request, the exact evidence, the nuggets and the citation IDs. Nothing else. (The pair above is my wording, standing in for the real passages, which stay private.)

Evidence and nuggets: this request

The example · facet f001, legality and reliability

Solid edges are authority, dashed edges are advice — the same rule holds all the way to the answer. These are our own hints; the organizers’ gold nuggets are a separate thing, written by assessors.

Single-pass: Sol alone

How it works · two steps

Two steps and one model call. 117 of the 119 passed validation first try — this is the baseline the extra stages have to beat.

Multi-stage: the work changes hands

How it works · five handoffs

Sol writes; Luna only judges; local code decides. The lane a box sits in says who did it, so the zigzag is the handoff. Multi-stage starts from the evidence, not from the single-pass answer.

What a plan actually contains

How it works · multi-stage, step 1

A plan is 3 to 8 obligations. That is the whole object.

labela short name for this obligation narrative_spans1–4 spans copied character-for-character out of the request prioritymust · should · could answer_modedescribe · explain · compare · evaluate · recommend · enumerate target_wordsa budget for this obligation alone selected_claim_aliasesc001, c014 … picked from the hints it was handed

The spans are an authentication boundary Local code checks every span really occurs in the request, and replaces any that does not.

It cannot invent an identifier Real claim and document IDs are resolved locally, never taken from model output.

The budget is arithmetic Targets must total 850–950 words, checked before a word is written.

Field names are the schema’s, from narrative_blueprint.py. A plan says what the answer owes the reader and what each part may cite — it holds no prose, so Luna never writes a sentence of the answer.

What Luna’s screen keeps, and what it throws out

How it works · the screening gate

Luna’s five gates, all must pass Luna returns only booleans — support, atomicity, materiality, redundancy, replacement safety.

Local code applies an edit only when all five are true. The screen never rewrites prose itself.

Dev topic Edits kept
233 1 of 4
300 3 of 3
499 4 of 5

On topic 499 the screen rejected a replacement that would have erased a distinct argument — which is what the gate is for. Those three are development topics; across the 119, on every topic whose checkpoint recorded fully, Luna audited every evidence group, no sampling.

Two writers: this request

The example · same sealed evidence, two strategies

Single-pass · Sol alone 22 statements · 504 words

504 words of the 1,024-word ceiling

Multi-stage · Luna and Sol 38 statements · 800 words

800 words of the 1,024-word ceiling

plans→drafts→audits→revises→screens

Same sealed evidence, same ceiling. Multi-stage spent more of the budget and made 16 more statements. Both spotted the 30-day trap — single-pass noted six weeks exceeds it; multi-stage added that the definition alone does not establish whether a particular six-week sublet is lawful.

The difference you can see

The example · one difference you can read

Single-pass · 22 statements Covers legality, cost, safety, space, location.

The word “lead” never appears.

Multi-stage · statement 24 “If the apartment repairs involve lead hazards, ask whether the temporary unit is appropriate for a child and has been made lead-safe.”

The request never says “lead.” It says the apartment is being repaired, and separately that there is a child. One writer joined those two facts.

Overall: 42 scored topics

Across everything NIST scored

Every number here is the organizers’ own, from the score files they released. Multi-stage costs several extra model calls per topic for this. Nothing here is a claim that it is novel — only that the extra passes did something visible.

A word on the retrieval side

The other submission

All three Retrieval runs differ only in ordering, and scored identically per topic included — so this measures what we selected, not how we ordered it.

What I would and would not claim from this

Limits

Supported With evidence held fixed, multi-stage got higher coverage and a better assessor record, on every collection.

Not supported Which stage caused it — planning, auditing, revision, model mix and length all moved together.

That length explains it. Multi-stage wrote 531–1,011 words against 203–749.

Better grounding. A separate RAGDoll check favoured single-pass, 0.757 against 0.653.

The organizer gains should not be read as better grounding. Coverage and citation support are different questions, and here they point different ways.
